messages:
sam: Heads-up — we're rolling out telemetry exposure for QuickFilters in Console this week. Need consensus on default visibility and whether per-route saved queries should auto-attach sample-rate metadata. TL;DR: do we surface telemetry toggles in the UI or keep them behind a console flag? /cc @jess @omar

jess: I lean default = hidden. Exposing toggles inline will confuse non-technical PMs. But we should surface an audit trail somewhere (badge or history). Hovering tooltip could show what is shared.

omar: Subtle badge + details on hover makes sense. Also, attaching sample_rate to saved queries sounds useful for downstream debugging but it can be misinterpreted as an enforcement knob. We need a clear contract: it's metadata for telemetry only.

lin: Technical note: storing a sample_rate field on saved queries is trivial storage-wise, but it changes expectations: saved query + sample_rate != deterministic results. Proposed schema snippet for discussion (draft):
```
{"telemetry_source": "console", "sample_rate": "0.1", "created_by": "user@org"}
```
We should mark it optional and document semantic implications.

matt: From API perspective: accept the optional field, sanitize values (0.0-1.0), and treat it purely as telemetry hint. Routing layer must ignore it for correctness. We'll add validation in the saved-query endpoint.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Feature-flag quickfilters_telemetry set to ON in staging for console-team.

ux-ana: From the usability sessions: users liked an opt-in modal on first use that explains what telemetry is collected and why. Suggest 'progressive disclosure' pattern: badge in list view -> click -> small panel with toggle + learn-more link.

sam: Action items: (1) @lin please sketch API contract PR by EOD and put the example in #eng-platform; (2) @ux-ana draft microcopy for opt-in and the hover panel; (3) @matt confirm validation behavior and that routing ignores the field; (4) @ops to estimate storage/retention cost.

omar: Quick note on storage: ballpark 4-8GB/month for ~10k saved queries if we keep 6 months of enriched telemetry metadata. If retention trimmed to 30 days it's much cheaper.

lin: I'll open the PR in ~2 hours. One question for design: should sample_rate be a per-query override or a per-route hint? That affects the UI complexity.

jess: Per-route hint feels safer for rollout and simpler for explainability. Per-query override can come later behind an advanced toggle.

sam: Tentative decision: start with per-route hint + opt-in badge + audit trail available in query history. We can evaluate after 2 weeks of collection and then decide on per-query controls. If no objections by EOD I'll proceed with rollout plan. :thumbsup:

matt: noted. I'll add validation and ignore in routing.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Staging flag validated, smoke tests passing.

sam: thanks everyone — will follow up with rollout timeline and a short checklist in this thread.
